historical_admission_evidence.component_acceptance_note: Exact existing packet evidence is bound; this inventory does not independently reaccept every partial proof or establish novelty.
historical_remaining_work_not_silently_a: The original unmarked group characterization, chiral cases and orders 2^k p remain outside these conclusions. Exact unrestricted excess-three counts are now supplied by a complete finite graph and integer-vector certificate; higher excess coefficients remain uncomputed. This is progress on a restricted component, not a solution of Problem 30 or a rederivation of the survey. Publication priority, complete formalization and a matched proof-length ratio remain unestablished.
historical_admission_evidence.summary: Problem 30, printed p.19: restricted regular two-group components: Canonical bounded cores classify ordered nondegenerate regular two-group markings at fixed excess. A global marked-kernel basis gives every class-at-most-three marking in every rank, with a two-state transfer formula and Fibonacci total. Separated first-excess cores give the unrestricted leading coefficient 5^k/k! and a lower-degree higher-class contribution.; Companion complete excess-two ordered-marking classification: For d>=3, exactly (25d^2-107d+122)/2 nondegenerate ordered string C-group markings of order 2^(2d+1). Of these 9d-20 have class four: 4d-8 with cyclic gamma3, and 5d-12 with elementary-abelian gamma3. The exact constructions and marked presentations establish completeness. Lean verifies the nested-kernel IP adapter under its explicit profile assumptions, not the full classification. The independent rank-three quotient census is a bounded diagnostic. No additional principal-paper credit or priority claim.; Companion finite-state classification at every fixed nilpotency class: For fixed c>=2, ordered nondegenerate finite two-group string C-groups of class at most c correspond exactly to accepted walks in an effectively finite graph of c-windows and boundary deletion kernels. Compatible semidirect/diagonal gluing, coset Helly and exact deletion update prove construction, actual IP and uniqueness. The rank/excess generating function is rational. At excess k>=1, class<=k+2 and windows of order<=2^(3k+3) suffice. No efficient general library enumeration, unmarked/chiral classification or full Problem30 resolution is claimed.; Companion exact third-excess ordered-marking count in every rank: For rank d>=4 and order2^(2d+2), a3(d)=(125d^3-855d^2+2380d-2646)/6; rank3 has37. All706 rank-five windows give708 states and1522 edges. The exact2832-coordinate identity (T-I)^4 v7=0 gives an alternate all-rank proof without the eventual-polynomiality input. Ranks4–6 use separate exact bases. GAP/NQ and the finite-state completeness theorem remain inputs; no unmarked or reversal count, whole-problem solution or priority claim.

question_dispositions.paraphrase: Classify self-dual toroidal polyhedra.
question_dispositions.qualification: The spherical classification is attributed background; regular or chiral toroidal maps are only a subclass.

question_dispositions.paraphrase: Decide whether every equivelar self-dual polyhedron has a polarity.
question_dispositions.qualification: The source gives the affirmative regular/chiral subclass and a negative unrestricted self-duality example; neither answers the equivelar question.

question_dispositions.paraphrase: Classify fully transitive polyhedra on surfaces of small genus, with both orientability choices.
question_dispositions.qualification: The toroidal classification cited in the source includes a further family whose middle adjacency preserves each flag orbit.

question_dispositions.paraphrase: Determine the least orientable genus at least two admitting a nonregular fully transitive polyhedron.
question_dispositions.qualification: The source excludes chiral maps in genera two through six; fully transitive is a larger class.

question_dispositions.paraphrase: Characterize groups of fully transitive polyhedra outside the regular and chiral classes.
question_dispositions.qualification: The subsequent self-dual restriction is an additional suggested subproblem.

question_dispositions.paraphrase: Classify edge-transitive polyhedra on orientable and nonorientable surfaces of small genus.
question_dispositions.qualification: The cited partial results do not give the requested classification.

question_dispositions.paraphrase: Determine what all specified hole and zigzag lengths determine, and when the associated universal regular quotient is finite.
question_dispositions.qualification: The first question covers regular or chiral polyhedra of type {p,q}, with 1<=j<=floor(q/2). The universal regular quotient in the subsequent question is distinct. Word-order formulas alone give neither uniqueness nor a universal finiteness criterion.

question_dispositions.paraphrase: Decide existence with prescribed regular or chiral facets and vertex figures.
question_dispositions.qualification: This is already negative in general in the source: the cited toroidal (3,0) facet and hemicube vertex figure have no regular amalgamation.

question_dispositions.paraphrase: Characterize the compatible facet and vertex-figure pairs for which amalgamation exists.
question_dispositions.qualification: Matching their common sections is necessary but insufficient.

question_dispositions.paraphrase: Determine universal groups and their finiteness for regular facet and vertex-figure pairs admitting amalgamation.
question_dispositions.qualification: The source existence theorem for the universal object is retained separately from group classification.

question_dispositions.paraphrase: Determine universal groups and finiteness for oriented chiral/regular amalgamations with at least one chiral member.
question_dispositions.qualification: Choose enantiomorphic forms, with at least one chiral constituent and every regular constituent directly regular. Simultaneous reversal identifies four oriented choices in pairs; if one constituent is regular the remaining choices also agree. Existence remains a prerequisite.

question_dispositions.paraphrase: Determine existence and finiteness with an arbitrary finite regular facet and a convex regular vertex figure.
question_dispositions.qualification: The source records the cross-polytope vertex-figure case: finiteness is equivalent to neighborliness of the facet.

question_dispositions.paraphrase: Determine existence and finiteness with finite chiral facets and convex regular vertex figures.
question_dispositions.qualification: The regular cross-polytope result does not automatically extend to chiral facets.

question_dispositions.paraphrase: Establish existence of finite chiral polytopes in ranks at least six.
question_dispositions.qualification: Affirmative answer conjectured in the 2006 source. This inventory makes no present-day open-status assertion.

question_dispositions.paraphrase: Decide whether a convex four-polytope can have every facet combinatorially icosahedral.
question_dispositions.qualification: An abstract polytope or incidence geometry with such facets is not sufficient.

question_dispositions.paraphrase: Classify universal regular amalgamations of square toroidal maps with odd distinct parameters s,u at least three.
question_dispositions.qualification: Two claims are embedded: existence for every such pair and finiteness only for (3,5) and (5,3).

question_dispositions.paraphrase: Classify universal regular amalgamations of triangular and hexagonal toroidal maps in the stated regular parameter families.
question_dispositions.qualification: Retain the exact source parameter domains: s>=2,t=0 or s=t>=1, and the corresponding u,v alternatives.

question_dispositions.paraphrase: Complete the classification of the three locally toroidal universal regular rank-six families, up to duality.
question_dispositions.qualification: The completeness of each finite list and the explicit one-relation infinite-family conjecture are separate clauses.

question_dispositions.paraphrase: Classify the universal locally toroidal chiral rank-four polytopes with the specified regular or chiral constituents and enantiomorphic forms.
question_dispositions.qualification: The preceding discussion and subsequent group calculation focus on the finite classification; retain that goal separately from the literal universal-object wording. At least one constituent is a chiral toroidal map. The square-torus/cube subfamily has its own four-pair finiteness conjecture.

question_dispositions.paraphrase: Classify finite universal regular or chiral rank-four polytopes with prescribed small facet and vertex-figure genera and orientabilities.
question_dispositions.qualification: Duality exchanges the two mixed orientability cases; the problem is not restricted to locally toroidal polytopes.

question_dispositions.paraphrase: Develop the realization theory of chiral polytopes.
question_dispositions.qualification: A theory of equivariant Gram matrices alone does not classify faithful realizations or determine their full geometric symmetry.

question_dispositions.paraphrase: Describe realization cones of regular toroids in every rank.
question_dispositions.qualification: The cited rank-three cones are established background, not the requested all-rank description.

question_dispositions.paraphrase: Decide whether a finite string C-group can have a complex irreducible character with Frobenius-Schur indicator minus one.
question_dispositions.qualification: The representation must be quaternionic; a general real representation or a non-C-group example is insufficient.

question_dispositions.paraphrase: Determine intersection-property validity from character tables or other readily computed group-algebra invariants for a marked string-generated group.
question_dispositions.qualification: The marking is part of the input. An explicit subgroup enumeration is not by itself an answer to the character-data question.

question_dispositions.qualification: Regular and chiral classifications supply subclasses only.

question_dispositions.qualification: The four classes are: products of cubes and crosspolytopes; products of cubes or crosspolytopes and 4k-gons (k>=1); uniform convex polytopes; regular star-polytopes. Affirmative answers are conjectured for classes 1,2,4; class 3 remains a separate question.
